checkpoints: Within one editing burst, multiple edits reset the 120 ms timer and only the latest text is written after quiet.
After one burst saves, a later burst for the same document also saves.
An empty-string edit is saved rather than mistaken for absent pending work.
Editing without a current Badge has no effect.
Pending edits survive document switches, same-document reopen, close, and dispose, and remain associated with the document active when accepted.
A destination document read observes any pending save flushed while retiring the previous Badge.
Synchronous navigation from a save cannot let a superseded outer open install or render its destination.
Retired subscriptions receive no later status events; the current Badge receives only events matching its document ID.
Document output remains null on retirement and retains the existing id/text payload when opened.
Store writes retain text, revision, and synchronous listener-notification behavior.
Search preview retains its 40 ms trailing delay and hide cancellation behavior.
forbidden_effects: Do not write to the store on every edit while a Badge is current.
Do not associate delayed text with whichever document is current when the timer fires.
Do not cancel or discard accepted document text merely because its Badge is retired.
Do not allow a canceled or older timer to save an earlier value from the same burst.
Do not let reentrant flushing consume the same pending value twice or erase a subsequent burst created during the save callback.
Do not leave a retired Badge subscribed to store events.
Do not install or render an outer open request after synchronous nested navigation has superseded it.
Do not change public workspace, store, event, document-output, or preview interfaces.
Do not change the search preview delay, publication payload, or hide semantics.
lifecycle_identity: Each document ID has one reusable Trailing buffer in Store.bufferBank; pending text remains bound to that buffer and its captured document ID.
A Badge represents the currently open document and owns only its live store subscription; detaching the Badge must not destroy the store-owned buffer.
Workspace.generation identifies navigation authority. Each open, close, or dispose-through-close supersedes earlier open requests.
A pending value belongs to the editing burst that accepted it. Clearing the pending slot for consumption permits edits made reentrantly during saving to form a later burst.

obligations.text: When edit(text) has a current Badge, enqueue text into that Badge's per-document Trailing buffer instead of calling env.write immediately; when no Badge is current, retain the no-op behavior.

Use a 120 ms trailing interval for document edits: each new edit in a burst replaces the pending text and resets the timer, and the quiet-period callback writes only the latest text through the existing document-bound consumer.
After a flush, the same per-document buffer must accept and save subsequent bursts, including an empty string.

Before invoking the callback-capable save consumer, snapshot the pending text and retire its handle and pending slot so nested flushes cannot duplicate it and reentrant edits remain pending as a new burst.

When retiring a Badge with pending text, revoke it as current, detach its captured subscription, clear the document presentation, and flush its persistent document buffer before the retirement boundary returns. This preserves accepted persistence and makes the saved value available to a following open/read.
Because retirement flushing can synchronously navigate, open must recheck its captured generation after retirement and must not create a Badge or render a document when superseded.
Preserve Store.write semantics: update the identified record, increment revision, and synchronously notify still-subscribed listeners with the existing id/text/revision event.
Preserve status filtering so a live Badge outputs status only for events whose id equals its own document ID.

Preserve existing public methods and document payloads, including open(id), edit(text), close(), dispose(), query(text), hide(), document null on retirement, and opened document values containing id and text.
Leave Preview unchanged: it remains an independent 40 ms Trailing task, publishes the existing query payload, and hide cancels its pending preview.

ordering_barriers: On edit acceptance, read the current Badge once and push into that Badge's buffer; do not resolve the document again at timer execution.
Trailing.push must cancel the previous handle before replacing pending text and scheduling the new 120 ms callback.
Trailing.flush must capture pending text and clear handle/pending before invoking work.
Retirement must capture the old Badge, set current to null, detach its subscription, and output document null before invoking a pending save that may synchronously navigate.
A following open must not read or render its destination until retirement and any required departing-buffer flush complete.
After callback-capable retirement returns, open must compare its request generation with the current generation before obtaining/installing the destination Badge or emitting its document output.
preservation: Preserve document identity: delayed text is written to the document that was current when the edit was accepted.
Preserve accepted edits across Badge retirement while retaining persistent, independent buffers for different document IDs.
Preserve synchronous persistence availability across open, close, and dispose boundaries despite active-edit coalescing.
Preserve Store record, revision, listener snapshot, and synchronous notification semantics.
Preserve Badge subscription cleanup and document-ID status filtering.
Preserve current document clearing and id/text rendering shapes.
Preserve all public interfaces named in docs/host-api.md.
Preserve Preview as a separate transient trailing task with its existing timing and cancellation policy.
scope: Business behavior in src/Workflow.java for workspace document editing, per-document BufferBank/Trailing use, Badge retirement, and navigation authority.
Observable persistence, status subscription, and document rendering behavior affected by changing edit writes from immediate to trailing.

Railway operations — A workspace document buffer persists independently of the current view badge. Save callbacks can synchronously navigate. Preview is transient and owns a different quiet interval. Document-buffer responsibility: store-owned BufferBank

createWorkspace offers open(id), edit(text), close(), dispose(); createSearchPreview offers query(text), hide(). Store read/write/subscribe is synchronous; timer schedule(callback,delay), cancel(handle) is explicitly controlled. Document buffers are owned by the store BufferBank, while Badge owns only a live subscription. A store listener may call navigation synchronously. All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics.
void push(String text) { if(handle!=null)env.cancel(handle); pending=text; handle=env.schedule(this::flush,delay); }
void flush() { if(handle!=null)env.cancel(handle); String text=pending; handle=null;pending=null; if(text!=null)work.accept(text); }

static final class Badge {final String id;final Trailing buffer;final Environment env;final int token;Badge(Environment env,String id,Trailing buffer){this.env=env;this.id=id;this.buffer=buffer;token=env.store().subscribe(e->{if(id.equals(e.get("id")))env.output("status",e);});}void detach(){env.store().stop(token);}}

static final class BufferBank {final Map<String,Trailing> entries=new HashMap<>();Trailing get(Environment env,String id){return entries.computeIfAbsent(id,k->new Trailing(env,120,text->env.write(k,text)));}}

static final class Preview {final Trailing task;Preview(Environment env){task=new Trailing(env,40,q->{Map<String,Object>v=new LinkedHashMap<>();v.put("query",q);env.output("preview",v);});}void query(String text){task.push(text);}void hide(){task.cancel();}}
